p: it came to pass: Paul, not being offended at the rudeness of the Ephesians, plants a church amongst them.
Holy Ghost since ye believed: Those excellent gifts of the Holy Spirit, which were in the Church in those days.
And he said unto them: John only began to instruct the disciples whom Christ would make perfect.
what then were ye baptized: In what doctrine then are you taught and instructed?
John's baptism: To be baptized into John's baptism is to profess the doctrine which John preached and to be identified with his baptism.
But when divers were hardened: For a man to separate himself and others from infidels who are utterly desperate, is not to divide the Church, but rather to unite it, and make it one.
way before the multitude: By this word "way", the Hebrews understand any type of life, and here it is taken for Christianity.
Tyrannus: This was a man's proper name.
Then certain of the vagabond Jews: Satan is forced to give witness against himself.

exorcists: So were they called who cast out demons by forcing them to leave in the name of God: and in the beginning of the Church, those who had the gift of working miracles, and laid their hands on those that were possessed with demons, were called the same.
prevailed against them: He prevailed against them, though they struggled ever so much.
And many that believed came: Conjuring and sorcery is condemned by open testimony, and by the authority of the apostle.
confessed: Confessed their errors, and openly detested them, being terrified with the fear of the judgment of God: and how does this compare to confession to a priest?
fifty thousand pieces of silver: Those that give the lowest estimate, reckon it to be about eight hundred pounds English.
After these things were ended: Paul is never weary.
spirit: By the motion of God's Spirit: therefore we may not say that Paul ran rashly unto death, but as the Spirit of God led him.
And the same time there arose: Gain cloaked with a show of religion is the very cause why idolatry is strongly and stubbornly defended.
shrines for Diana: These were special counterfeit temples with Diana's picture in them, which those who worshipped her bought.
this our craft is in danger: As if he said, "If Paul goes on in this way as he has begun, to confuse the opinion which men have of Diana's image, all of our gain will come to nothing."

And certain of the chief of: There ought to be in all Christians, and especially in the ministers, an invincible steadfastness which may not by any storms or assaults be overcome, which nonetheless must modestly allow itself to be governed by wisdom.
But when they knew that he: Instead of reason, the idolaters are sufficiently contented with their own madness and outcries, and those are the greatest defence that they have.
And when the townclerk had appeased: An example of a political man who redeems peace and quietness with lies, which Paul would have never done.
fell down from Jupiter: The Ephesians believed superstitiously that the image of Diana came down to them from heaven.
matter against any man: Have anything to accuse any man of.
law is open: For there are certain days appointed for civil causes and matters of judgment, and the deputies sit on those days.
deputies: By the deputies are meant also the deputies' substitutes, that is, those who sat for them.

lawful assembly: He speaks of a lawful assembly not only to speak against the disordered tumult of the people, but also against all meeting and coming together which was not by order: for there were certain days appointed to call people together in.
